clue.text: Stuck up small head by mistake

parts.note: nob is old slang for the head
bish is British slang for a blunder or mistake

explanation.surface: Someone acting superior has trimmed a small head off by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: BISH is informal British slang for a mistake, and NOB an old slang word for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stuck up means acting superior to others, which is what a snobbish person does.

clue.text: Kills merriment aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard says the merriment is carried inside the ship

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the usual crossword ship
laughter is merriment

explanation.surface: Someone murders the fun on board a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: SS, steamship, is the standard crossword ship; 'aboard' signals that the merriment is placed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To slaughter is to kill, especially in large numbers.

clue.text: Public dismissal is too much

parts.note: overt means open, public
axing is a sacking, a dismissal

explanation.surface: A public sacking is going a step too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word; the definition is 'too much' in the sense of excessively demanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overtaxing makes excessive demands, asking too much of someone.

clue.text: Do butchers extract all nutritious offal first of all?

indicators.note: first of all says each following word gives only its opening letter

explanation.surface: Do butchers remove all the nutritious offal before anything else?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like the start of a question but is a noun: a party, a beano in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A beano is British slang for a party or celebration, which is also called a do.

clue.text: Frame guides showing ways to access multiple places

parts.note: a skeleton is a frame or framework
keys are guides, as a key explains a map

explanation.surface: A framework of guides shows ways into several places.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton key opens many different locks, so it gives access to multiple places.

clue.text: Uproar behind you and me

parts.note: the behind is the rump, the backside
you and me together are us

explanation.surface: A commotion is going on behind two people's backs.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy disturbance or commotion, a synonym of uproar.

clue.text: Suggestion from subordinate, tense individual

parts.note: under means lower in rank, subordinate
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A tense junior staff member makes a suggestion.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertone is an underlying hint or implication, a suggestion of something.

clue.text: Support lord vocally

indicators.note: vocally says the word for lord is to be heard, not read

parts.note: a peer is a lord in the House of Lords

explanation.surface: Backing a member of the nobility out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a pillar or column that holds up a structure, a support.

clue.text: Cook ineffectual politicians upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue says the word is turned over, bottom to top

parts.note: wets was Thatcher's name for feeble moderate Conservatives

explanation.surface: Ineffectual politicians are cooked and upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wets' was Margaret Thatcher's term for moderate, weak Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: To stew food is to cook it slowly in liquid.

clue.text: State has plenty of time and means

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
ages is a long time, as in 'it took ages'

explanation.surface: A state is said to have plenty of time and money at its disposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'means' is a plural noun here: averages are means in statistics, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics a mean is an average, so averages are means.

clue.text: Stick poster in this place

parts.note: a poster is an advertisement, an ad
in this place means here

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a poster up right here.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast to something, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Republican and Democrat droned on about keeping house plant

indicators.note: keeping says the two parties hold the house between them
about says the letters of droned on are moved around

explanation.surface: Politicians from both parties droned on about a potted shrub in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' has the two party letters hold the house abbreviation; 'about' rearranges DRONED ON. 'house plant' tempts as one phrase, but only 'plant' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhododendron is a flowering evergreen shrub, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Meet and greet ghetto revolutionary

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns things over, so these letters are overturned into a new order

explanation.surface: A revolutionary from the ghetto is going to a meet-and-greet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meet and greet' looks like a single phrase, but 'Meet' alone is the definition; 'revolutionary' rearranges GREET GHETTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A get-together is an informal gathering, a meeting of people.

clue.text: Clumsy American couple thrive without Flo

parts.note: to mate is to couple, to pair up

indicators.note: without says the name Flo is taken out

parts.note: to flourish is to thrive
taken as written

explanation.surface: An awkward American couple manage to thrive without Flo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes FLO from FLOURISH, leaving URISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateurish work is unskilled and inept, so clumsy is a near synonym.

clue.text: Factor in dirt engine churned up

indicators.note: churned up says these letters are stirred into a different order

explanation.surface: A factor in the mess: dirt churned up by an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingredient is one element or component of something, which is what a factor is.

clue.text: Poisonous beast consumed by jerk

indicators.note: consumed by says the beast is swallowed inside the jerk

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary jerk
an ox is a beast of burden

explanation.surface: A venomous animal is eaten by some fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' looks like a fool but is a twitch, a tic.
explanation.definitionFit: Toxic substances are poisonous ones; the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Loudly regret returning after tea with posh driver

indicators.note: after says the loud regret comes behind the tea and posh

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
U means upper-class, posh
FF, fortissimo, means very loudly in music

indicators.note: returning says the word for regret is read backwards

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Regretting loudly, a posh driver comes back after tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses the regret word; 'after' puts the loud regret behind tea and posh. U for upper-class and CHA for tea are old British usages.
explanation.definitionFit: A chauffeur is someone employed to drive a car for others.

clue.text: Following overdose music producer, born in Sultanate, finds fixer

indicators.note: following says the next piece comes straight after the overdose

parts.note: a DJ, disc jockey, produces music at a club

indicators.note: in says born sits inside the sultanate

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate in Arabia

explanation.surface: After an overdose, a record producer born in Oman discovers who fixed things.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd-job man does small repairs around the house, so he is a fixer.

clue.text: Searched and managed to fire journalist

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it, so ran means managed
to sack someone is to fire them
ED, editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Someone went through the office and managed to fire a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack a place is to search it thoroughly and roughly.

clue.text: Begin letter without introduction

indicators.note: without introduction says the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a letter is one who lets property, which is one sense of renter

explanation.surface: Advice on starting a letter without any opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' is not a written message but someone who lets out property, a renter; 'without introduction' drops its R.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter on something is to begin it, as when entering a new phase.

clue.text: Brief special vehicle branch of the police

parts.note: a flying visit is a brief one
a quad is a quad bike, a four-wheeled vehicle

explanation.surface: A short-lived special vehicle unit within the police force.
explanation.walkthrough: The Flying Squad is a London Metropolitan Police unit dealing with armed robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: The Flying Squad is a specific unit, a branch, of London's police.

clue.text: Second party for rascal

parts.note: a camp is a group or party with shared views

explanation.surface: A second party is held for a mischievous child.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a mischievous person, a rascal.

clue.text: Women behind drift

parts.note: aft means behind, at the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: Women trailing behind are drifting along.
explanation.definitionFit: To waft is to float or drift gently through the air.

clue.text: Stun and partially confound a zealot

indicators.note: partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Instructions to stun and partly confuse a fanatic.
explanation.definitionFit: To daze someone is to stun or stupefy them.

clue.text: Arouse interest in article about vigil

indicators.note: about says the article goes around the vigil

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a wake is a vigil kept over a body before burial

explanation.surface: Getting people interested in an article written about a vigil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the article around the vigil; a wake is the watch kept over a body before a funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: To awaken feelings or curiosity is to stir them up, so it means to arouse interest.

clue.text: Original member of family left out after bit of controversy

indicators.note: after says the shortened relative follows that letter
bit of means only the opening letter of controversy is used
out says the letter for left is removed

parts.note: a relative is a member of the family

explanation.surface: A family member with fresh ideas walked out after a spot of controversy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' removes L from RELATIVE to give REATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A creative person or work is original and inventive; the words are near synonyms.

clue.text: Attempt to embrace man with love in ideal situation

indicators.note: to embrace says the attempt wraps its arms around what follows

parts.note: a try is an attempt
he is the pronoun for a man
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Trying to embrace a loving man in a perfect setting.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'in theory', meaning in an ideal world rather than in practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Theory, as opposed to practice, describes how things work in an idealised world.

clue.text: Stretches back to get steamy photograph

indicators.note: back says the word for stretches is read backwards

parts.note: spans are stretches of distance or time
steamy means hot

explanation.surface: Someone stretches backwards to take a racy picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a quick, informal photograph.
